key_insight: RIDAR detects research integrity violations in autonomous research agents and intervenes during execution to reduce violations remaining at task completion.
engineering_relevance: Agent developers can use RIDAR to audit research trajectories and add runtime safeguards for validity, reproducibility, and faithfulness.
method: Define RIVT, a taxonomy of 14 research integrity violation types spanning the research lifecycle.
Apply RIDAR-post-hoc to detect violations in recorded agent trajectories.
Use RIDAR-runtime to dynamically detect and correct violations during execution.
evidence_signal: RIDAR-post-hoc achieved 85.2% F1 on 60 expert-annotated trajectories and detected 3,964 violations in 99.7% of 300 trajectories across 50 tasks; runtime intervention reduced remaining violations by 36.8%.
watch_item: Detection is imperfect, and the abstract does not report runtime overhead or intervention effects on research task performance.
paper_title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
